items.notes: Check that all four cases share one value on every dimension (Ashcombe Primary, Year 4, autumn, Vance) and that the only things varying are start dates, measurement dates and point gains. The closer names the halved class sizes and then blocks them: every class took its English lessons in fixed groups of six, so the roll size cannot reach the teaching, and the tail rules out anything else. That is what makes a same-class year-on-year comparison adequate here.

items.confound_note: All four classes are Year 4 groups at Ashcombe Primary in one autumn term taught by Vance, and the single fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: class sizes at each school ran about a quarter below the year before. The scope clause beside that fact has every logged class taking its English lessons as one whole group, which puts every lesson in front of a smaller room than in the term the class is measured against. Each class is compared against itself in the previous autumn term, under the larger rolls. The evidence cannot separate the smaller classes from the reading program. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the scores covering every pupil on roll; no second defect is present.
items.notes: Cases must be byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. The halved class sizes work as a confound ONLY because the four cases share a school and a term, and they reach the classes because every one took its English lessons as one whole group. Both closer clauses are reused elsewhere in the family - the class-size fact also appears in coherent_true and the scope clause also appears in diverse_true - so the contrast is a conjunction, not a vocabulary difference.

items.confound_note: In cases one, three and four the comprehension score was recorded before the program began: 11 September precedes 6 December at Ashcombe Primary, and 24 April precedes 20 June at Halloway Junior. Three quarters of the evidence therefore describes gains that were already in place when the classes started the program, so it cannot be evidence for the program. The two remaining cases, Deerpark Academy and Marchfield Grange, are too few to establish the claim on their own.
items.notes: The closer shares its fact clause with diverse_true and its scope clause with coherent_true, so neither clause marks the label; the conditions are verbatim identical to diverse_true. The ONLY substantive change from diverse_true is the month in two date pairs in cases one and three, so the token bag is unchanged and the flaw is invisible lexically. Check that exactly two cases are reversed and that cases two and four remain in correct order.
